[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard defines the mandatory requirements for scaffolding, registering, and managing the lifecycle of Terraform deployment environments in Gainwell product repositories. It establishes the architecture approval prerequisites that must be satisfied before any environment can be scaffolded, specifies the required directory structure and file inventory for each environment, mandates environment registration in `.project.yml` as the authoritative environment registry, defines short naming conventions, governs locals file references to cloud configuration, and establishes the first-deployment protocol and multi-region deployment rules.
page_texts.6:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#scope]

### Scope

**In scope**: All Terraform deployment environment directories under `iac/terraform/deployments/aws/` in Gainwell product repositories. This standard governs environment creation, naming, directory structure, locals file references, `.project.yml` registration, and pipeline integration requirements for every environment from `dev` through `prd`.

**Out of scope**: The content of Terraform module configurations (governed by STD-INFRA-IAC-002). The CD pipeline that deploys to these environments (governed by STD-INFRA-IAC-010). Platform Gainwell infrastructure (pfe-pg) environments not owned by product teams. AWS account vending (governed by the Cloud Governance standard).
page_texts.7:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

**Mandatory.** No environment directory may be created, deployed to, or added to the CD pipeline dispatch options without satisfying every requirement in this standard. Environments scaffolded without architecture approval, `.project.yml` registration, or the required directory structure are ungoverned and cannot receive deployments through the standard CD pipeline.
page_texts.8:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Ad-hoc environment creation — directories added without registration, incomplete file structures, incorrect locals references, or unreviewed architecture — creates deployment failures, security configuration gaps, and state management problems that are difficult to diagnose after the fact. Requiring architecture approval before scaffolding ensures infrastructure decisions trace to reviewed design. Registration in `.project.yml` provides a single authoritative environment inventory that all tooling (CI, CD, health-check scripts) can rely on. The mandatory file structure ensures every environment is deployment-ready from the first use and eliminates "environment partially scaffolded" failures during first deployment.

[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#req-iac-011-01-architecture-approval-before-environment-scaffolding]

#### REQ-IAC-011-01: Architecture Approval Before Environment Scaffolding

Both the conceptual architecture AND the logical architecture for the product **must** be approved before any environment directory may be scaffolded.

- **REQ-IAC-011-01a**: Conceptual architecture approval is evidenced by an approved conceptual architecture document in `docs/design/conceptual/` with CRB sign-off recorded in the Change Review Board log. A draft or in-review conceptual architecture does not satisfy this requirement.
- **REQ-IAC-011-01b**: Logical architecture approval is evidenced by an approved logical architecture document in `docs/design/logical/` with ARB sign-off recorded in the Architecture Review Board log. A draft or in-review logical architecture does not satisfy this requirement.
- **REQ-IAC-011-01c**: The environment scaffolding PR **must** reference the approved conceptual and logical architecture documents in the PR description. The reviewer **must** verify that architecture approval is in place before approving the scaffolding PR.
- **REQ-IAC-011-01d**: Architecture approval is assessed at the product level, not per environment. Once conceptual and logical architectures are approved for a product, all environments for that product may be scaffolded without re-approval unless the architecture is materially revised.

**Rationale**: Infrastructure decisions — VPC placement, security group topology, network attachment patterns, state backend configuration — must trace to approved architecture. Scaffolding environments before architecture is approved creates infrastructure that may be inconsistent with the eventual approved design, resulting in costly rework. The architecture approval gate ensures every environment is built on a reviewed, authorized design.
page_texts.12:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#req-iac-011-02-environments-must-be-registered-in-projectyml-before-scaffolding]

#### REQ-IAC-011-02: Environments Must Be Registered in `.project.yml` Before Scaffolding

Every environment **must** be registered in `.project.yml` under `iac.environments_nonprod` or `iac.environments_prod` before the environment directory is created and before any deployment is executed.

- **REQ-IAC-011-02a**: Nonprod environments (`dev`, `test`, `prf`) **must** be listed under `iac.environments_nonprod` in `.project.yml`.
- **REQ-IAC-011-02b**: Production environments (`cfg`, `sit`, `uat`, `prd`) **must** be listed under `iac.environments_prod` in `.project.yml`.
- **REQ-IAC-011-02c**: The `.project.yml` registration **must** be committed in the same PR as the environment directory scaffolding. A PR that creates the directory without updating `.project.yml` must be rejected.
- **REQ-IAC-011-02d**: The CD pipeline `cd-deploy.yml` **must** derive its allowed environment list from `.project.yml` at runtime (see STD-INFRA-IAC-010 REQ-IAC-010-10b). An environment not in `.project.yml` **must not** appear in the dispatch input options.

**Rationale**: `.project.yml` is the single authoritative source of truth for the environment inventory of a product repository. All tooling — CI validators, CD pipeline inputs, health-check scripts, the `/infra-env-create` skill — reads from `.project.yml` to understand what environments exist. An environment that exists on disk but is not in `.project.yml` is invisible to all tooling and cannot be managed through standard processes.

[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#req-iac-011-03-deployment-zone-must-be-confirmed-active-before-scaffolding]

#### REQ-IAC-011-03: Deployment Zone Must Be Confirmed Active Before Scaffolding

The deployment zone (pfe-pg zone) for the environment **must** be confirmed as active in the pfe-pg platform before scaffolding begins.

- **REQ-IAC-011-03a**: Deployment zone confirmation is obtained from the Platform Gainwell team by filing a zone readiness request referencing the environment short name and the AWS account/region target.
- **REQ-IAC-011-03b**: The zone readiness confirmation **must** be referenced in the scaffolding PR description (ticket number, confirmation email, or ADO work item link). A PR without zone confirmation evidence must be rejected.
- **REQ-IAC-011-03c**: If the deployment zone does not exist or is not active, the product team **must** coordinate with Platform Engineering to provision the zone before proceeding with environment scaffolding. This step is a prerequisite, not a parallel activity.
- **REQ-IAC-011-03d**: `acquire-tfstate` (the first step of the CD pipeline) will fail if the deployment zone is not active. Scaffolding an environment in an inactive zone produces a directory structure that cannot be deployed. This requirement prevents that class of failure.

**Rationale**: Platform Gainwell manages the foundational networking and state backend infrastructure that product environments depend on. An environment scaffolded against an unprovisioned or inactive zone will fail at the first CD pipeline run when `acquire-tfstate` attempts to retrieve zone outputs. Confirming zone availability before scaffolding ensures the environment is deployable from day one.

[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#req-iac-011-04-required-file-inventory-for-each-environment-directory]

#### REQ-IAC-011-04: Required File Inventory for Each Environment Directory

Each environment directory **must** contain the following files. A directory missing any required file is incomplete and cannot be deployed.

- **REQ-IAC-011-04a**: `locals-env.hcl` — environment-specific local variables (short name, tier, region, tags). References the appropriate cloud locals file (see REQ-IAC-011-06).
- **REQ-IAC-011-04b**: `acquire-tfstate/terragrunt.hcl` — Terragrunt configuration for the `acquire-tfstate` step. This file defines the remote state backend reference for the pfe-pg zone outputs consumed by all subsequent steps.
- **REQ-IAC-011-04c**: `deploy-common/common-includes.hcl` — shared include block for common Terraform provider and backend configuration, sourced from the product's `iac/terraform/common/` directory.
- **REQ-IAC-011-04d**: `deploy-common/security-groups.hcl` — Terragrunt configuration for the security-groups formation. Defines the product's security group resources for this environment.
- **REQ-IAC-011-04e**: `deploy-common/security-group-rules.hcl` — Terragrunt configuration for the security-group-rules formation. Defines the inbound and outbound rules for the security groups defined in `security-groups.hcl`.
- **REQ-IAC-011-04f**: `deploy-common/terragrunt.hcl` — root Terragrunt configuration for the deploy-common step. Includes `common-includes.hcl` and declares the dependency chain: `acquire-tfstate` → `security-groups` → `security-group-rules`.

**Rationale**: The six required files represent the minimum viable environment configuration. `acquire-tfstate/terragrunt.hcl` and the `deploy-common/` files are always required because every product environment needs platform state (subnets, VPC, accounts) and network security baseline (security groups + rules). An environment directory missing any of these files cannot run `cd-deploy.yml` successfully. The required file list is the contract between the scaffolding step and the deployment pipeline.
page_texts.15:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#req-iac-011-05-environment-short-names-required]

#### REQ-IAC-011-05: Environment Short Names Required

Environment directory names **must** use the approved short names. Full English names are prohibited.

- **REQ-IAC-011-05a**: Approved short names: `dev`, `test`, `prf`, `cfg`, `sit`, `uat`, `prd`.
- **REQ-IAC-011-05b**: Full-word names (`development`, `testing`, `performance`, `configuration`, `staging`, `user-acceptance`, `production`) are **prohibited** as directory names.
- **REQ-IAC-011-05c**: Variants, abbreviations, or aliases not in the approved list (e.g., `prod`, `stage`, `qa`, `perf`, `uat1`) are **prohibited** without an Architecture Exception and `.project.yml` registration under the non-standard name.
- **REQ-IAC-011-05d**: The short name used in the directory path **must** match the name registered in `.project.yml` exactly (case-sensitive). Mismatches cause `cd-deploy.yml` validation to fail.

**Rationale**: Consistent short names are a required prerequisite for all downstream tooling. The CD pipeline derives `DEPLOYMENT_PATH` from the environment short name input. `acquire-tfstate` is invoked with `$(basename $DEPLOYMENT_PATH)`. Health-check scripts, the `/infra-env-create` skill, and the architecture health-check all use these names. Non-standard names break tooling expectations and require per-team exceptions in every tool that references environment names.
page_texts.16:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#req-iac-011-06-locals-envhcl-must-reference-the-correct-cloud-locals-file]

#### REQ-IAC-011-06: `locals-env.hcl` Must Reference the Correct Cloud Locals File

`locals-env.hcl` **must** include the appropriate cloud locals file based on the environment tier.

- **REQ-IAC-011-06a**: Nonprod environments (`dev`, `test`, `prf`) **must** include `locals-cloud-nonprod.hcl`. Including `locals-cloud-prod.hcl` in a nonprod environment is **prohibited**.
- **REQ-IAC-011-06b**: Prod environments (`cfg`, `sit`, `uat`, `prd`) **must** include `locals-cloud-prod.hcl`. Including `locals-cloud-nonprod.hcl` in a prod environment is **prohibited**.
- **REQ-IAC-011-06c**: Cross-referencing the wrong cloud locals file creates deployments where nonprod workloads can accidentally reference prod network infrastructure, or prod workloads reference nonprod state backends. CI linting **must** validate this reference as part of environment scaffolding review.
- **REQ-IAC-011-06d**: The cloud locals file path **must** use a relative path from `locals-env.hcl` to the shared `locals-cloud-nonprod.hcl` or `locals-cloud-prod.hcl` in `iac/terraform/common/`. Absolute paths are **prohibited**.

**Rationale**: `locals-cloud-nonprod.hcl` and `locals-cloud-prod.hcl` contain different AWS account IDs, VPC references, and state backend configurations for their respective tiers. Mixing them creates a hybrid deployment where, for example, a dev workload provisions resources into the production VPC. This is a high-severity misconfiguration that has caused PHI-scope incidents in other healthcare organizations. The explicit requirement and its CI lint enforcement eliminate this class of error.
page_texts.17:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#req-iac-011-07-cd-deployyml-must-be-updated-for-new-environments]

#### REQ-IAC-011-07: `cd-deploy.yml` Must Be Updated for New Environments

After scaffolding a new environment, `cd-deploy.yml` **must** be updated to include the new environment in the workflow dispatch `environment` input choice list.

- **REQ-IAC-011-07a**: The `cd-deploy.yml` update **must** be included in the same PR as the environment scaffolding. A scaffolded environment that is not in the dispatch options cannot be deployed through the standard pipeline.
- **REQ-IAC-011-07b**: The new environment name in the `cd-deploy.yml` choice list **must** match the short name registered in `.project.yml` exactly.
- **REQ-IAC-011-07c**: When removing an environment (end-of-life), `cd-deploy.yml` **must** have the environment removed from the dispatch options in the same PR that removes the environment directory. A decommissioned environment that remains in dispatch options can be triggered accidentally.
- **REQ-IAC-011-07d**: The `cd-deploy.yml` environment choice list **must not** contain environment names that do not exist in `.project.yml`. Stale entries in the choice list create deployment attempts against nonexistent directories.

**Rationale**: A deployment pipeline that cannot target an environment is not useful. The scaffolding PR is the correct moment to add the environment to the pipeline — when the directory exists, the architecture is approved, and the zone is confirmed active. Adding environments to the dispatch list as a separate later PR creates a window during which the environment exists but cannot be deployed through the governed pipeline, tempting engineers to use manual `terragrunt apply` invocations instead.
page_texts.18:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#req-iac-011-08-first-deployment-must-run-with-skipinfrafalse]

#### REQ-IAC-011-08: First Deployment Must Run with `skip_infra=false`

The first execution of `cd-deploy.yml` for a newly scaffolded environment **must** run with `skip_infra=false` (or equivalent) to ensure `acquire-tfstate` and `deploy-common` both execute.

- **REQ-IAC-011-08a**: `acquire-tfstate` and `deploy-common` are infrastructure steps that establish the network security baseline (security groups and rules) for the environment. These steps **must** execute on first deployment, even if the product team intends to deploy only the application workload.
- **REQ-IAC-011-08b**: If the CD pipeline supports a `skip_infra` dispatch input that bypasses `acquire-tfstate` and `deploy-common`, that option **must** default to `false` and **must not** be used for the first deployment of a new environment.
- **REQ-IAC-011-08c**: The scaffolding PR documentation **must** include a note reminding the team to run the first deployment with `skip_infra=false`. A checklist item in the PR template is an acceptable mechanism.
- **REQ-IAC-011-08d**: Subsequent deployments may use `skip_infra=true` to skip the infrastructure steps if only application changes are being deployed and infrastructure state has not changed.

**Rationale**: `deploy-common` provisions the security groups and security group rules that control network traffic for the environment. If the first deployment skips `deploy-common`, the workload is deployed into an environment with no security group baseline — allowing all traffic or blocking all traffic depending on the VPC default. Either outcome is incorrect and the former is a security violation in a PHI-handling environment. Mandating `skip_infra=false` on first deployment ensures the security baseline is always established before the workload goes live.
page_texts.19:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#req-iac-011-09-acquire-tfstate-must-complete-before-deploy-common]

#### REQ-IAC-011-09: `acquire-tfstate` Must Complete Before `deploy-common`

`acquire-tfstate` **must** complete successfully before `deploy-common` runs. This dependency is enforced in the pipeline and cannot be made optional.

- **REQ-IAC-011-09a**: `cd-deploy.yml` **must** declare `needs: acquire-tfstate` on the `deploy-common-plan` job. Running `deploy-common` without the `acquire-tfstate` dependency is a pipeline configuration violation.
- **REQ-IAC-011-09b**: `deploy-common` requires the outputs of `acquire-tfstate` (VPC ID, subnet IDs, remote state references) to resolve Terragrunt `dependency` blocks. If `acquire-tfstate` has not run in the same pipeline execution, `deploy-common` will fail with unresolved dependency references.
- **REQ-IAC-011-09c**: `acquire-tfstate` **must not** be cached between pipeline runs. Each pipeline execution acquires fresh platform state to ensure it reflects any platform-level changes that occurred since the last run.
- **REQ-IAC-011-09d**: The `deploy-common-apply` job **must** re-run `acquire-tfstate` independently (see STD-INFRA-IAC-010 REQ-IAC-010-03). Environment variables set in the plan job's `acquire-tfstate` step are not forwarded to the apply job (separate runner instances).

**Rationale**: GitHub Actions jobs execute on separate runner instances. Environment variables, files, and state set in one job are not automatically available in another. The `acquire-tfstate` outputs that `deploy-common` depends on must be acquired within the same job execution. Running `acquire-tfstate` in both plan and apply jobs independently ensures both operations use current, live platform state — protecting against state changes that occur in the platform between the plan run and the apply run.
page_texts.20:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#req-iac-011-10-primary-region-always-deploys-secondary-region-only-when-required]

#### REQ-IAC-011-10: Primary Region Always Deploys; Secondary Region Only When Required

The primary AWS region always deploys for every environment. The secondary region deploys only when multi-region is required for that specific environment.

- **REQ-IAC-011-10a**: Every environment **must** deploy to the primary region. The primary region is defined in `locals-cloud-nonprod.hcl` or `locals-cloud-prod.hcl` and **must not** be overridden per environment without an Architecture Exception.
- **REQ-IAC-011-10b**: Secondary region deployment is only required when the environment's logical architecture specifies multi-region availability (e.g., active-active HA, disaster recovery with automated failover). Development and test environments (`dev`, `test`, `prf`) **must not** deploy to a secondary region unless explicitly required by the architecture with ARB approval.
- **REQ-IAC-011-10c**: When secondary region deployment is required, `locals-env.hcl` **must** define `secondary_region_enabled = true`. When it is not required, `locals-env.hcl` **must** define `secondary_region_enabled = false` or omit the variable (defaults to false).
- **REQ-IAC-011-10d**: The `cd-deploy.yml` `region` input **must** accept both the primary and secondary regions. When `secondary_region_enabled = false`, the pipeline **must** reject a deployment targeting the secondary region for that environment and fail with: "Secondary region deployment is not enabled for environment '${{ inputs.environment }}'".

**Rationale**: Secondary region deployments double the cost of infrastructure resources and increase operational complexity. Making secondary region deployment opt-in per environment (rather than the default for all environments) prevents accidental cost escalation in lower environments. Requiring ARB approval for multi-region in nonprod ensures that the cost and complexity is justified by a genuine availability requirement, not a default misconfiguration.

[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- **Use `/infra-env-create` skill for scaffolding**: The `/infra-env-create` skill generates the required file structure, updates `.project.yml`, and creates the scaffolding PR with all required checks. Manual scaffolding is error-prone.
- **Include environment short name in all tags**: Tag all AWS resources with `Environment = <short-name>` (e.g., `Environment = dev`) to enable cost allocation and resource inventory by environment.
- **Scaffold nonprod before prod**: Always scaffold and validate `dev` before scaffolding `cfg`. Use `dev` to confirm the scaffolding is correct before creating prod-tier environments.
- **Document per-environment deviations**: If an environment requires a deviation from the standard directory structure (e.g., an additional Terragrunt configuration not in the required inventory), document the deviation in the environment directory's `README.md`.

---
page_texts.22:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

| Prohibited Practice | Reason |
|---------------------|--------|
| Scaffolding before architecture approval | Infrastructure not traceable to reviewed design |
| Creating environment directories without `.project.yml` registration | Environment is invisible to all tooling |
| Full-word environment names (`production`, `staging`, etc.) | Breaks all tooling that relies on short name contract |
| Including `locals-cloud-prod.hcl` in a nonprod environment | Nonprod workloads can reference prod infrastructure |
| Including `locals-cloud-nonprod.hcl` in a prod environment | Prod workloads reference nonprod state backends |
| Adding environment to `cd-deploy.yml` before `.project.yml` | Pipeline can target unregistered environments |
| Running first deployment with `skip_infra=true` | Security group baseline is not established |
| Deploying to secondary region in nonprod without ARB approval | Unnecessary cost; not justified by availability requirement |
| Hardcoding environment-specific paths in locals files | Non-portable; breaks when environment is renamed |

---
page_texts.23:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. **REQ-IAC-011-01 (architecture approval prerequisite)**: Time-bounded exceptions (maximum 30 days) are available for proof-of-concept environments where architecture is in active development. PoC environments **must** be named `poc` and **must not** contain PHI. All PoC resources must be destroyed before the permanent environment is scaffolded.
2. **REQ-IAC-011-05c (non-standard short names)**: Additional environments beyond the standard seven require an Architecture Exception with ARB sign-off and a justification for why the standard names are insufficient.
3. **REQ-IAC-011-10b (secondary region in nonprod)**: Requires a documented multi-region availability requirement in the logical architecture with ARB approval. Pre-approved for `prd` environments in products with a DR requirement.
4. All other exceptions require a formal Architecture Exception with ARB sign-off.

### Required Environment Directory Structure

```text
iac/terraform/deployments/aws/<env-short-name>/
├── locals-env.hcl                          # REQ-IAC-011-04a
├── acquire-tfstate/
│   └── terragrunt.hcl                      # REQ-IAC-011-04b
└── deploy-common/
    ├── common-includes.hcl                 # REQ-IAC-011-04c
    ├── security-groups.hcl                 # REQ-IAC-011-04d
    ├── security-group-rules.hcl            # REQ-IAC-011-04e
    └── terragrunt.hcl                      # REQ-IAC-011-04f
```
page_texts.26:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#required-locals-envhcl-template]

### Required `locals-env.hcl` Template

```hcl
# iac/terraform/deployments/aws/<env-short-name>/locals-env.hcl

locals {
  env_short_name = "<env-short-name>"          # Must match directory name and .project.yml entry
  env_tier       = "<nonprod|prod>"            # nonprod: dev/test/prf  |  prod: cfg/sit/uat/prd

  # REQ-IAC-011-06: reference correct cloud locals file based on tier
  # nonprod environments:
  cloud_locals = read_terragrunt_config(find_in_parent_folders("locals-cloud-nonprod.hcl"))
  # prod environments (replace the line above with this):
  # cloud_locals = read_terragrunt_config(find_in_parent_folders("locals-cloud-prod.hcl"))

  # REQ-IAC-011-10c: secondary region (false for dev/test/prf; conditional for prod)
  secondary_region_enabled = false

  # Tagging
  tags = {
    Environment = local.env_short_name
    ManagedBy   = "terraform"
    Product     = local.cloud_locals.locals.product_name
  }
}
```

page_texts.32:
[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#implementation-requirements]

### Implementation Requirements

1. **Confirm prerequisites**: Verify conceptual and logical architecture are approved. File a zone readiness request with Platform Engineering for the target environment.
2. **Register in `.project.yml`**: Add the environment short name to `iac.environments_nonprod` or `iac.environments_prod` in the same PR as the scaffolding.
3. **Create directory structure**: Use the `/infra-env-create` skill (preferred) or manually create the required files per the template in Technical Specifications.
4. **Set `locals-env.hcl`**: Reference the correct cloud locals file (`locals-cloud-nonprod.hcl` or `locals-cloud-prod.hcl`) per tier.
5. **Update `cd-deploy.yml`**: Add the environment to the `environment` input choice list in the same PR.
6. **Open scaffolding PR**: Include references to approved architecture documents and zone confirmation evidence in the PR description.
7. **Run first deployment with `skip_infra=false`**: After the scaffolding PR merges, trigger `cd-deploy.yml` with `skip_infra=false` to establish the security group baseline.

### Scaffolding PR Checklist

The following items **must** be confirmed in the scaffolding PR before merge:

- [ ] Conceptual architecture approved (reference document path and CRB confirmation)
- [ ] Logical architecture approved (reference document path and ARB confirmation)
- [ ] Deployment zone confirmed active with Platform Engineering (reference ticket/email)
- [ ] Environment registered in `.project.yml`
- [ ] All six required files present in environment directory
- [ ] `locals-env.hcl` references correct cloud locals file for the tier
- [ ] `cd-deploy.yml` updated with new environment in dispatch choice list
- [ ] PR reviewer confirms four-eyes review of above checklist

[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#testing-requirements]

### Testing Requirements

- **Structural validation test**: Run `find iac/terraform/deployments/aws/<env>/` and confirm all six required files are present.
- **`.project.yml` registration test**: Run the repo health-check script and confirm the new environment is listed in the environment inventory.
- **First deployment test**: Trigger `cd-deploy.yml` with `skip_infra=false`. Confirm `acquire-tfstate` and `deploy-common` both execute and complete successfully.
- **Cloud locals reference test**: Run a `terraform validate` for the environment and confirm no errors referencing wrong account IDs or VPCs (sign that the wrong cloud locals file was referenced).
- **Dispatch input test**: Confirm the new environment appears in `cd-deploy.yml` dispatch options and can be successfully targeted.

[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#monitoring-requirements]

### Monitoring Requirements

Platform Engineering runs a weekly automated inventory check that compares environment directories in `iac/terraform/deployments/aws/` against `.project.yml` registrations. Unregistered directories (present on disk but missing from `.project.yml`) are flagged in the governance dashboard as "ungoverned environments" and escalated to the product team.

The scaffolding PR template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`) **must** include the scaffolding checklist defined in the Implementation Guidelines section. PR automation checks that the checklist items are checked before the PR is mergeable.

### Exception Handling

- PoC environment exceptions (REQ-IAC-011-01): Filed via ADO work item tagged `iac-exception-poc`. Platform Engineering tracks PoC environment lifecycles and enforces teardown after 30 days.
- Non-standard environment name exceptions (REQ-IAC-011-05c): Require Architecture Exception with ARB sign-off and a `.project.yml` entry under a custom key (`iac.environments_custom`).

- **Standards Owner**: Platform Engineering — owns the scaffolding templates, `/infra-env-create` skill, and environment lifecycle processes.

[standards/infrastructure/iac/STD-INFRA-IAC-011-environment-scaffolding.md#example-2-incorrect-cloud-locals-reference-and-how-to-catch-it]

#### Example 2: Incorrect Cloud Locals Reference (and How to Catch It)

**Context**: An engineer scaffolds a `sit` (prod) environment and accidentally includes `locals-cloud-nonprod.hcl` in `locals-env.hcl`.

**Detection**:

- PR reviewer checks `locals-env.hcl` diff and sees `locals-cloud-nonprod.hcl` referenced for a `sit` (prod-tier) environment — flagged in review.
- If merged and deployed, `terraform validate` would return account ID mismatches; `deploy-common` would fail when attempting to create security groups in the nonprod VPC.
- CI lint automation (see STD-INFRA-IAC-006) **should** include a check that `sit`/`uat`/`cfg`/`prd` directories reference `locals-cloud-prod.hcl`.

**Resolution**: PR is rejected. Engineer updates `locals-env.hcl` to reference `locals-cloud-prod.hcl`, adds a PR comment explaining the correction, and re-requests review.
